From c35636e91e392e1540949bbc67932167cb48bc3a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Oliver Hartkopp <socketcan@hartkopp.net>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 11:58:06 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] can: bcm: fix locking for bcm_op runtime updates

Commit c2aba69d0c36 ("can: bcm: add locking for bcm_op runtime updates")
added a locking for some variables that can be modified at runtime when
updating the sending bcm_op with a new TX_SETUP command in bcm_tx_setup().

Usually the RX_SETUP only handles and filters incoming traffic with one
exception: When the RX_RTR_FRAME flag is set a predefined CAN frame is
sent when a specific RTR frame is received. Therefore the rx bcm_op uses
bcm_can_tx() which uses the bcm_tx_lock that was only initialized in
bcm_tx_setup(). Add the missing spin_lock_init() when allocating the
bcm_op in bcm_rx_setup() to handle the RTR case properly.

Fixes: c2aba69d0c36 ("can: bcm: add locking for bcm_op runtime updates")
Reported-by: syzbot+5b11eccc403dd1cea9f8@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-can/699466e4.a70a0220.2c38d7.00ff.GAE@google.com/
Signed-off-by: Oliver Hartkopp <socketcan@hartkopp.net>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260218-bcm_spin_lock_init-v1-1-592634c8a5b5@hartkopp.net
Signed-off-by: Marc Kleine-Budde <mkl@pengutronix.de>

diff --git a/net/can/bcm.c b/net/can/bcm.c
index b7324e9c955b..fd9fa072881e 100644
--- a/net/can/bcm.c
+++ b/net/can/bcm.c
@@ -1176,6 +1176,7 @@ static int bcm_rx_setup(struct bcm_msg_head *msg_head, struct msghdr *msg,
 		if (!op)
 			return -ENOMEM;
 
+		spin_lock_init(&op->bcm_tx_lock);
 		op->can_id = msg_head->can_id;
 		op->nframes = msg_head->nframes;
 		op->cfsiz = CFSIZ(msg_head->flags);
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies a single file, `net/can/bcm.c`, to fix a locking issue in the Broadcast Manager (BCM) module.

**Modifications:**
- In the `bcm_rx_setup()` function, added `spin_lock_init(&op->bcm_tx_lock)` to properly initialize the spin lock for a newly allocated BCM operation (`bcm_op`). Previously, this lock was only initialized in `bcm_tx_setup()`, but it is also needed for RX operations that can transmit CAN frames (when the `RX_RTR_FRAME` flag is set), as they call `bcm_can_tx()` which uses this lock.

**Relationships:**
- The added initialization ensures that the `bcm_tx_lock` is always valid before any operation (RX or TX) attempts to acquire it. This fixes a bug where an RX operation could try to use an uninitialized spin lock, leading to undefined behavior or crashes. The fix completes the locking introduced in commit c2aba69d0c36 ("can: bcm: add locking for bcm_op runtime updates") by covering the previously missed initialization path.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>op = kzalloc(OPSIZ, GFP_KERNEL);
// missing: spin_lock_init(&op->bcm_tx_lock);</text>
<text>// Later, when RX_RTR_FRAME is set, bcm_can_tx() uses op->bcm_tx_lock.</text>
<text>// bcm_tx_setup() has spin_lock_init(&op->bcm_tx_lock); but bcm_rx_setup() does not.</text>
Reason:
The spin lock `op->bcm_tx_lock` was only initialized in `bcm_tx_setup()`, not in `bcm_rx_setup()`. When an RX operation with the `RX_RTR_FRAME` flag is created, it uses `bcm_can_tx()` which relies on this lock, leading to usage of an uninitialized spinlock and potential undefined behavior.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>+		spin_lock_init(&op->bcm_tx_lock);</text>
<text>placed after `op = kzalloc(OPSIZ, GFP_KERNEL);` in `bcm_rx_setup()`.</text>
Reason:
Adding `spin_lock_init(&op->bcm_tx_lock)` when allocating a new `bcm_op` in `bcm_rx_setup()` ensures the spinlock is properly initialized before any use, fixing the bug where an uninitialized lock was used when handling RTR frames via `bcm_can_tx()`.
